title: Logical Access Security Measures
description: The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets to protect them from security events to meet the entity's objectives.
key_requirements: Identify and authenticate users prior to granting access
Restrict access to authorized users and processes
Implement controls to prevent unauthorized access
Manage access credentials (provisioning, modification, revocation)
common_evidence: Offboarding checklist with access revocation timestamps

aws_implementation.guidance: Use AWS IAM Identity Center for centralized access management with MFA enforced. Create IAM policies using least-privilege principles. Enable CloudTrail to log all API calls. Use AWS Config rules (e.g., iam-user-mfa-enabled, iam-no-inline-policy) for continuous monitoring. Conduct access reviews using IAM Access Analyzer.

common_failures: Shared accounts / service accounts used by humans
MFA not enforced for all users (especially privileged)
Access reviews performed but not documented with owner sign-off
Terminated employees with delayed access revocation (>24 hours)
Overly permissive IAM policies (e.g., wildcard actions)
auditor_red_flags: Gap between termination date and access revocation date
No evidence of periodic access reviews
Root account used for day-to-day operations
No MFA on privileged or production accounts

title: Monitoring of Security Events
description: The entity monitors system components and the operation of those controls on an ongoing basis to identify anomalies that are indicative of malicious acts, natural disasters, and errors affecting the entity's ability to meet its objectives.
key_requirements: Monitor system components for anomalous activity
Detect potential or actual security events
Alert on indicators of compromise
Review and investigate alerts
common_evidence: Evidence of alert review (tickets, incident logs)

aws_implementation.guidance: Enable GuardDuty across all accounts and regions for threat detection. Aggregate findings into Security Hub. Create CloudWatch alarms for critical API calls (e.g., root login, security group changes). Ensure CloudTrail is enabled with log file validation and shipped to a separate, immutable S3 bucket. Set log retention to meet policy requirements (typically 1 year).

common_failures: GuardDuty enabled but findings never reviewed or triaged
Alerts configured but no escalation path defined
CloudTrail not enabled in all regions
Log retention insufficient for audit period
No evidence that alerts were investigated (no tickets/runbooks)
auditor_red_flags: High-severity GuardDuty findings with no remediation record
Alert fatigue — hundreds of unreviewed findings
Security Hub scores never reviewed by a human

title: Vendor and Business Partner Risk Management
description: The entity assesses and manages risks associated with vendors and business partners.
key_requirements: Identify critical vendors and subservice organizations
Assess vendor risk prior to onboarding
Review vendor SOC reports or conduct assessments
Monitor vendor risk on an ongoing basis
Include security requirements in vendor contracts
common_evidence: Reviewed vendor SOC 2 reports with management response

aws_implementation.guidance: Use AWS Artifact to obtain AWS compliance reports (SOC 2, ISO 27001). Maintain a vendor register in a GRC tool or structured spreadsheet. For vendors with AWS environments, request their SOC 2 Type II report. Establish a recurring calendar process for annual re-review. Use contract templates with standard security annexes.

common_failures: No formal vendor inventory maintained
SOC reports collected but not reviewed for exceptions or qualifications
No re-assessment process for existing vendors
Fourth-party risk not considered
DPAs missing for vendors with access to personal data
auditor_red_flags: Critical vendors with no SOC report or assessment on file
Vendor SOC reports more than 12 months old
No management response to vendor SOC exceptions

title: Information Classification
description: Information shall be classified in terms of legal requirements, value, criticality, and sensitivity to unauthorised disclosure or modification.
key_requirements: Classify information according to a defined classification scheme
Label information assets consistently
Handle information according to its classification level
Define classification roles and responsibilities
common_evidence: Data classification scheme (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted)
Examples of labeled documents or assets

aws_implementation.guidance: Use Amazon Macie to automatically discover and classify sensitive data (PII, credentials) in S3. Implement mandatory resource tagging policy with a 'data-classification' tag enforced via AWS Config or Service Control Policies (SCPs). Define tag values aligned to your classification scheme. Use S3 bucket policies to enforce controls based on classification tags.

common_failures: Classification policy exists but not consistently applied
No data inventory with classification levels assigned
Classification scheme too complex — staff don't use it
Macie enabled but findings not actioned
No handling requirements defined per classification level
auditor_red_flags: Policy says 'all data must be classified' but no evidence it happens
Sensitive data found in unclassified or public-facing systems
No training records showing staff understand classification requirements

category: Protect: Identity Management and Access Control
title: Identities and Credentials
description: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited for authorized devices, users, and processes.
key_requirements: Maintain an authoritative identity store
Issue credentials using defined procedures
Revoke credentials when no longer needed
Audit credential lifecycle regularly
common_evidence: Identity provider (IdP) configuration (Okta, Azure AD, AWS IAM Identity Center)
Credential policy (password length, rotation, MFA requirements)

aws_implementation.guidance: Centralize identity management with AWS IAM Identity Center federated to your IdP (e.g., Okta). Enforce MFA at the IdP level. Use AWS Secrets Manager for programmatic credentials with automatic rotation. Define a formal JML (Joiner/Mover/Leaver) process with SLA for access revocation. Use CloudTrail + Athena queries to audit credential usage.

common_failures: Multiple identity silos with no central visibility
Long-lived access keys for service accounts without rotation
No formal JML process — access revocation is ad hoc
Privileged accounts not subject to stricter controls
auditor_red_flags: IAM access keys older than 90 days
Former employees found in access review with active credentials
